864bsk:275: The four models (user, task, world, self) do not exist independently; the coupling relationships among them are where the real value lies. The intersection of the user model and the world model determines preference applicability—when the user says "I like microservices," the validity of that preference in a specific organizational structure depends on that organization's service-boundary governance capability. The intersection of the task model and the self model determines the Agent's self-calibration ability—only by knowing which paths have failed in the past can it proactively avoid them during planning. The "intent" that emerges from this multi-model coupling is actually a high-dimensional latent variable that cannot be directly observed and can only be approximated through long-term coordination of multiple models. This explains why traditional key-value memory systems have never been able to produce reliable intent understanding—they lack a dynamic coupling layer between models.
